recA5BnM5umys9yRk.Body: Kyle and Serena Denton are community herbalists creating wild-crafted and organic plant medicines out of Milwaukee since 2015. I have used their teas and tinctures on an almost daily basis for years now. Kyle is a great friend of InnerVerse and has appeared on the channel more times than I can count. These products work—not in the allopathic "pharma-medicine" way, but in a terrain-support, consciousness bolstering plant-teacher sort of way.

recABS9cTyYGHFXEG.Body: The Sonic Slider is the flagship tool behind Biofield Tuning itself, a weighted tuning fork hand-tuned to 93.96 Hz, the twelfth harmonic of the Schumann Resonance, Earth's own natural electromagnetic pulse. Its extended handle lets you glide it smoothly across the face, neck, and body, and practitioners and users regularly report support for relaxation, circulation, and nervous system regulation. It's the same fork Chance uses in his own sessions, and a great entry point if you want to bring this work into your own daily routine.

recMVdJjP2VZJyI2m.Body: Clive de Carle has spent decades researching high-quality natural health essentials, from magnesium and fulvic minerals to iodine, selenium, and vegan-sourced vitamin D. His supplements are formulated with a focus on bioavailability, so the body can actually absorb and use what you're taking rather than letting it pass through unused. It's a simple, no-nonsense approach to filling the nutritional gaps most modern diets leave behind.
recMVdJjP2VZJyI2m.Name: Clive de Carle

rec7Vm5QNrDbc9sdb.Bio: Chance Garton is the host and producer of the Innerverse Podcast, where for over a decade he has investigated consciousness, mythology, symbolism, terrain health, and the psychosomatic language of the human body and mind. A biofield tuning practitioner, he uses tuning forks to help clients resolve physical symptoms, break negative patterns, and return to energetic coherence.
rec7Vm5QNrDbc9sdb.Name: Chance Garton
rec7Vm5QNrDbc9sdb.Role: Host of the Innerverse Podcast, biofield tuning practitioner & researcher

recBE7KwrPCyVVZMU.Bio: Gabriel, known on air as Slick Dissident, co-hosts InnerVerse's Vibe Rant show and is a longtime recurring guest on the podcast. He teaches occult symbolism and tarot on his YouTube channel, ranging across the Major Arcana, the esoteric Enneagram, mythology and archetype, mystic linguistics, and the symbolism hidden in popular film. He is best known for Tarot-tories, his own system mapping the 22 Major Arcana and zodiac archetypes onto the geography of the United States.
recBE7KwrPCyVVZMU.Name: Gabe (Slick Dissident)
recBE7KwrPCyVVZMU.Role: Co-host of Vibe Rant; teacher of occult symbolism & tarot

reczSXekaGaIOEEci.Bio: Chaney hosts the Project Chaney podcast, offering contrarian analysis of Hollywood symbolism, psychic/magical development, and mainstream narratives, with an emphasis on personal exploration over dogma.
reczSXekaGaIOEEci.Name: Chaney (Project Chaney)

fields.Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "The Placenta as Your Twin and Guardian", "body": "Gabe opens by reading the placenta as the place entered, the alpha that forms first and the omega that arrives last, and calls it a family heirloom and lost talisman born of the alchemical wedding of your parents. Chance reads how people in Indonesia treat the placenta as the baby's elder sibling and lifelong guardian that must be buried with ritual, and how the Maori use one word for both land and placenta. From there he proposes that, because it carries your full genetic code, it may hold a spirit of its own, a divine twin or holy guardian angel left lost at sea."}, {"title": "Birth Certificates, Names and Paper Identity", "body": "Gabe argues that everyday English hides the story in plain sight: the caul becomes what you are called, the mother signs the birth certificate as informant, and that living document, like an organ, is a collection of tissues with a common purpose that he says is used to track you. He extends the idea to the wallet, the driver's license with codes you cannot read, and the coded chits he says the Knights Templar gave pilgrims. Chance adds the 1302 papal bull Unam Sanctam from Boniface VIII, links salvation to salvage and savage, and suggests a two dimensional world of paper is trying to govern a three dimensional one."}, {"title": "Questioning Modern Hospital Birth", "body": "The three question how routine hospital birth handles the placenta and the mother. Gabe says the placenta is often cut early and shipped into an industry supplying medicine and cosmetics, pointing listeners to the research of Crow777. Chaney argues that C sections happen far more often than they need to because hospitals want to rush a natural process, and ties Caesar to what she sees as a swapping of Q for C. Chance suggests that birthing on the back adds trauma and raises the hypothesis, expanded with hypnosis accounts and rounded, organic craft interiors, that alien abduction memories may echo the birth room."}, {"title": "Reclaiming the Feminine in Symbols", "body": "Chaney argues that the feminine has been ripped out of religion and symbol across the board. She notes that eight Earth years match thirteen on Venus, suggests thirteen was branded unlucky because of its tie to women's cycles, and claims horned bull imagery borrows from Isis, adding her view that Mary Magdalene studied in an Isis school. The number 17, the Star card and the three spellings of Kabbalah with C, K and Q also come up. Chaney says a woman sitting with two men to talk about the placenta shows how far society has drifted, since three mothers should be having this conversation."}, {"title": "Companion Spirits, Daemons and The Shining", "body": "Chance reads from Pierre Sabak's Holographic Culture on the qareen, the companion spirit of Islamic tradition said to shape thought, and from Jung on his inner guide Philemon, then asks whether a voice in your mind that sounds like you might be your own twin. He invites listeners to recognize and reconnect with that lost part of themselves. Gabe offers his view that the daemon ages in reverse, drawing on The Shining played forward and backward at once, and says that in the novel Danny is born with a caul. Chance closes on the Karen meme, the cremation of care and a Transylvanian placenta custom."}]
fields.Intro Paragraph 1: I teamed up with Gabriel (Slick Dissident) and Chaney for a fully moon-charged & veil shredding conversation about the esoteric aspects of modern berth-rights, and how the hospital practices (especially regarding the placenta) that most parents take for granted are connected to the mysteries of royal bloodlines, the cosmic egg, Templars, Mary Magdalene, and world tree cosmology. It's an ambitious build but with these two syncromystic thinkers, I know we'll crack some skulls.
